PDF Guide · Getting started

How to merge PDF files in the correct order

Suppose you have a cover page, a report, and several supporting documents as separate PDFs. Sending them individually can confuse the reader, especially when file names are similar. Merging them into one document lets you create a predictable reading order and share a single attachment.

Before you merge: gather and check your files

Move the PDFs into a folder where you can see the names and recognize which should come first. Open the important files and confirm the pages are readable. If one PDF is password-protected, you will need a permitted unencrypted version before using PDFEasy. The tool will not bypass document protection.

Consider how the final document should flow. For a school assignment, this might be title page, assignment instructions, completed work, and references. For an office report, it could be summary, data analysis, and appendices. Think about the order before you choose files.

Step 1: select your PDF documents

Open the PDFEasy merge tool. Click the file selection button and choose at least two PDFs, or drop them into the highlighted upload area. The website checks each document in your browser and displays the file name and number of pages.

The current version allows up to 20 documents, no more than 30 MB each or 100 MB across the selection. These limits protect devices with less available memory. If you have larger documents, split your work into smaller batches or use a suitable desktop application.

Step 2: put the documents in order

The file list shows the exact sequence used during merging. You can drag a row to another position on devices that support dragging, or use the up and down buttons next to each file. The up and down buttons also make reordering easier when using a keyboard or touch device.

Make sure any cover page is first. Supporting material should follow the section it relates to. If you accidentally select an unrelated file, remove it from the list before merging.

Step 3: merge and download

Press “Merge & Download PDF.” The browser reads each selected document and copies its pages into a new PDF. The resulting document downloads as merged.pdf. Because the operation runs locally, your selected PDFs do not have to travel to a conversion server.

Large PDFs may take longer to process, especially on phones or devices with limited memory. Keep this tab open until the download begins. If something fails, try merging fewer documents at a time.

Step 4: verify the result

Open the downloaded file and inspect the first, middle, and last pages. Verify that the total page count looks right, the order is correct, and no pages have unexpected rotation. Check important images and text. A PDF merge can change advanced features: digital signatures, interactive forms, embedded attachments, and certain annotations may not behave as before.

If you are assembling a contract, bank form, or other document whose integrity is critical, do not assume the merged PDF preserves legal or cryptographic validity. Follow the document issuer's instructions instead.

Tips for a clean combined PDF

  • Use meaningful file names. “01-cover.pdf” and “02-report.pdf” are clearer than “final2.pdf”.
  • Check orientation. If a source document appears sideways, correct it in an appropriate editor before merging.
  • Avoid duplicate pages. Remove repeated source files unless intentionally including them twice.
  • Keep the source files. Save the originals separately in case the merged output needs revision.
  • Review sensitive content. Ensure you have permission to combine and distribute the documents.
